name: Minoan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Undeciphered ancient language (Linear A); no phonological description of stress exists. Glottolog: unclassifiable, no descriptive refs.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; summarizes vowel-system and syllable-structure debates, citing Salgarella 2025: 50 and Steele 2024: 16-20.

sources.citation: Steele, Philippa M. 2024 [OA 2023]. Exploring Writing Systems and Practices in the Bronze Age Aegean. Oxford/Philadelphia: Oxbow Books (CREWS series). Ch. 1, section 'Minoan phonology or other linguistic features?', pp. 13-18.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Discusses what can and cannot be reconstructed of Minoan phonology from Linear A/B sign correspondences: voicing/aspiration, the d-series vs /l/, labialised consonants, three- vs five-vowel system; explicitly counsels that 'we cannot know the phonetic reality' (p. 13). Cites Davis 2014: 193-245 as the most extensive reconstruction.

sources.citation: Packard, David W. 1974. Minoan Linear A. Berkeley/Los Angeles: University of California Press. Ch. 5 'Hints about the phonology of the Minoan language', pp. 112-119.
sources.note: Nothing. The chapter treats only the vowel inventory (weakness of the e and o series, possible three-vowel graphic system) and consonant series (d/l/r, palatalized/labialized series); no word on stress, accent or prosody (a full-text search for stress/accent: zero relevant hits).

sources.citation: Gordon, Cyrus H. 1966. Evidence for the Minoan Language. Ventnor, NJ: Ventnor Publishers. Sec. XI 'Minoan phonetics', paras 147-150 (p. 35).
sources.note: Nothing on Minoan stress. 'Minoan phonetics' covers vowel correspondences with (assumed) Semitic cognates, y-/aleph interchange, possible sibilant and l/r mergers, ayin > o. The only 'accent' mentions in the book (paras 68, fn. 42) concern Hebrew vowel reduction in the Eteocretan section, not Minoan.

sources.citation: Josefsson, Michael W. 2020. The Phonology of Minoan: Evidence from Linear A. Nuanced Garbling (University of Melbourne linguistics student journal) 2020: 8 pp.

tone.quote: The following chart summarises Minoan phonology. Sounds in brackets are typologically likely to have existed, on the basis of the behaviour of similar sounds, but are not directly evidenced above. [Table 5: Minoan phonology - consonant and vowel charts only] Drawing on previous efforts, this paper has attempted to present a brief original analysis of Minoan phonology, summarised above, by interpreting the irregularities of Linear B sounds as resulting from the mismatch between the sounds of Greek and the Minoan of Linear A.
tone.locator: p. 8, section 4 'Conclusion'; no tone/stress/prosody passage exists anywhere in the 8 pp.

sources.note: Title and citing context only; a typology-driven reconstruction of the segmental system (stop series, palatalised/labialised consonants, implosives) from Linear A/B sign behaviour; given the evidence base (a syllabary) it is very unlikely to state anything about tone or accent beyond, at most, that prosody is unrecoverable.
